description: Import historical transaction data and categories from Monarch Money CSV export. This seeds Family Pulse with 12+ months of categorized history, enabling meaningful budget baselines and trend analysis from day one. Migration is a one-time operation but must be repeatable and auditable.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 2 complete (category CRUD and transaction browser working). Monarch CSV export downloaded and inspected.

principles: Inspect the actual CSV before writing the parser — do not assume column layout
Category mapping is a human-guided process, not fully automated
Deduplication is critical — imported data must not conflict with Plaid-synced data
Every import run is logged and auditable
Monarch-sourced transactions always traceable via source='monarch' flag

techStack.testing: Jest with fixture CSV files for parser validation

userStories.title: CSV upload and parsing
acceptanceCriteria: Admin page with file upload for Monarch CSV
Parser handles Monarch export format (columns validated against actual export)
Preview mode: show first 20 rows parsed before committing import
Handles edge cases: quoted fields, commas in merchant names, empty categories
Upload stored in uploads/ directory with timestamp
File size limit enforced (10MB max)
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests with fixture CSV files (valid, malformed, edge cases). Parser output validated against expected transaction objects.

userStories.title: Category mapping UI
acceptanceCriteria: Extract unique Monarch categories from uploaded CSV
Display mapping table: Monarch category → Family Pulse category (dropdown)
Auto-suggest mappings using fuzzy string matching
Option to create new Family Pulse category inline if no match exists
Mapping saved and reusable for re-imports
Unmapped categories default to 'Uncategorized'
userStories.testStrategy: Fuzzy matching unit tests. UI test: mapping table renders, selections persist, new categories created inline.

userStories.title: Transaction import with deduplication
acceptanceCriteria: Import transactions with mapped categories, original dates, and amounts
Deduplication: skip if matching transaction exists (same date ± 1 day, same amount, same merchant substring)
Imported transactions flagged source='monarch' in database
Import runs in a database transaction — all or nothing on failure
Progress indicator during import (total, imported, skipped, errors)
userStories.testStrategy: Unit test for dedup logic (exact match, fuzzy date, partial merchant). Integration test: import CSV, verify DB records, re-import same CSV and confirm zero new records.

userStories.title: Import summary and audit
acceptanceCriteria: Import run recorded in import_runs table: filename, timestamp, record_count, skipped_count, error_count, status
Summary page after import: records imported, duplicates skipped, category mapping used, any errors
Admin view of import history (all past runs)
Imported transactions visible in transaction browser with 'Monarch' source badge
userStories.testStrategy: Integration test: verify import_runs record created with correct counts. UI test: summary page displays after import.

high: Monarch CSV format is undocumented — parser must be built from actual export inspection, not assumptions
Dedup logic too aggressive could skip legitimate transactions; too loose creates duplicates
medium: Category mapping quality affects all downstream budget analysis — bad mappings corrupt historical baselines
Large CSV imports (12+ months) may be slow — need progress feedback
low: Monarch may change export format before Eric downloads — low risk since download happens pre-development

preFlightChecklist: CRITICAL: Download Monarch CSV export and inspect actual column layout before writing parser
Identify Monarch category taxonomy — full list needed for mapping UI
Decide: import all historical transactions or only last N months?
Confirm: how does Monarch handle transfers in their export? Are they categorized or flagged?
